In addition, as the proposed development will undoubtedly include facilities having more than 250 employees, the so-called MASSPOOL regulation (s.52.1161) will also apply. Under this regulation, the employer would have to take a number of steps to ensure the minimization of single-occupant vehicles (SOC's) arriving at the facility. It should, however, be emphasized that although carpools are preferable to SOC's, arrivals by transit to this area would certainly be most preferable to arrival by any other vehicular mode.
(2) Emission Reductions Attributed to Motor Vehicle Emission Inspection and Maintenance Program
In the estimate of appropriate motor vehicle emission factors, it is assumed that an I&M program for all LDV's will be implemented by 1980 and, more importantly, that it will effectuate a 10% reduction in both CO and HC emissions. We certainly hope to be able to realize the assumed start-up target date of 1980, and, in fact, will devote a great deal of resources during the coming year to ensure the establishment of an effective I&M program as soon as possible. It is not clear, however, how the 10% emission reduction estimates were arrived at. As you may know, the realization of a 10% reduction will be possible only under a number of conditions, and over some period of time. These assumptions should be delineated further in the final EIS.
For a detailed discussion of appropriate techniques to generate reliable I&M emission reduction estimates, you are referred to "Appendix N-Emission Reductions Achievable Through Inspection and Maintenenace of Light Duty Vehicles, Motorcycles, and Light and Heavy Duty Trucks," 42 Federal Register 22177, May 2, 1977.
(3) Application of appropriate pollutant emission factors
Appropriately, the calculation of macroscale emissions relies heavily upon the most recent EPA motor vehicle emission factors. Unfortunately, however, the exhaust emission factors which were used in the air quality projections (Supplement 5 of AP-42, December 1975) have recently changed. Estimates based on data collected during 1975 and 1976 as part of EPA's emission factor program now indicate the 1975 Supplement 5 emission estimates to be significantly optimistic. More specifically, estimates based on available data now indicate that CO emissions, for example, are not only much higher than previously estimated, but also deteriorate more rapidly in subsequent years. The impact of these new emission factors should be investigated in the Final EIS, as they may seriously jeopardize the present conclusion that standards will be met in a timely manner. Similarly, the impact of the recent Clean Air Act Amendment deliberations on auto emission standards should also be fully explored in the Final EIS.
For your information, the "Revised Mobile Source Emission Factors" were issued by the EPA Assistant Administrator for Air and Waste Management on June 24, 1977.
